'''Hiroo Inokuchi''' (23 Feb 1927 – 20 March 2014) was a Japanese chemist who did pioneering work in electronic processes in organic materials, for which he received the 2007 [[Kyoto Prize in Advanced Technology]]. Since 2006, he was the chairman of the Japan Space Forum.

==Career==
Inokuchi contributed to many branches of the field of electronic processes in organic materials, including [[luminescence]], [[photoemission]], and [[spectroscopy]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Pope|first1=Martin|title=Professor Hiroo Inokuchi: a pioneer and major contributor to the field of electronic processes in organic materials|journal=Synthetic Metals|volume=64|issue=2-3|pages=109–113|doi=10.1016/0379-6779(94)90101-5|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Honors==
Inokuchi was a member of the Japan Academy and the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]. In 1965, the [[Japan Academy]] awarded him the [[Japan Academy Prize (academics)|Japan Academy Prize]]. In 1978 he received the Chemical Society of Japan Award from the [[Chemical Society of Japan]]. In 1994, the Japanese government recognized him as a [[Person of Cultural Merit]] and in 2001 they awarded him the [[Order of Culture]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Five pioneers to receive Order of Culture awards |url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2001/10/31/national/five-pioneers-to-receive-order-of-culture-awards/#.XDOIWi3TlSM |accessdate=7 January 2019 |work=The Japan Times Online |date=31 October 2001}}</ref> In 2007 he received the Kyoto Prize in Advanced Technology.<ref name=Kyoto_citation>{{cite web|title=Citation: Pioneering and Fundamental Contributions to Organic Molecular Electronics|url=https://www.kyotoprize.org/en/laureates/hiroo_inokuchi/ |website=The 2007 Laureates|publisher=The Inamori Foundation|accessdate=2 September 2014}}</ref>

The asteroid [[32270 Inokuchihiroo]], discovered in 2000, was named after Inokuchi.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |title=32270 Inokuchihiroo |last1=Schmadel |first1=Lutz D. |encyclopedia=Dictionary of minor planet names : addendum to 6th edition, 2012-2014 |date=2015 |publisher=Springer |isbn=9783319176772 |page=180}}</ref> In May, 2018, the Tokyo Physical and Chemical Research Institute opended the Hiroo Inokuchi Hall.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hiroo Inokuchi Hall just opened |url=https://www.inamori-f.or.jp/en/news/newsline/2018/08/02/3987/ |accessdate=4 January 2019 |work=News |agency=Inamori Foundation |date=2 August 2018}}</ref><ref name=Hall>{{cite web |title=Hiroo INOKUCHI Hall |url=https://www.toyotariken.jp/en/hall |website=Tokyo Physical and Chemical Research Institute |accessdate=7 January 2019 |language=ja}}</ref>
